NEWS 2026-11-20 The Droid Guy (How To Fix Handoff And Universal Clipboard On Mac (2026)):
Handoff and Universal Clipboard let you start something on an iPhone and finish it on a Mac, or copy on one device and paste on the other.
When they stop working, the Handoff icon does not appear in the Dock or the pasted content never arrives.
Apple lists the same short set of requirements for both features, so most fixes are a quick settings check.
Quick answer: what both features need
| Requirement | What Apple says | Where to check | 
|---|---|---|
| Same Apple Account | Every device must be signed in to iCloud with the same Apple Account | Settings on iPhone, System Settings on Mac | 
| Bluetooth and Wi-Fi | Both must be turned on for each device | Control Center or Settings | 
| Handoff switched on | Each device must have Handoff on; Apple says it is on by default | General settings on each device | 
| Nearby devices | Within 30 feet (10 meters) of one another | Physical distance | 
| Supported hardware and software | Devices must meet the Handoff or Universal Clipboard system requirements | Apple Continuity requirements page | 
Step 1: Turn Handoff on for every device
Universal Clipboard depends on Handoff, so a device with Handoff switched off breaks both features.
On a Mac running macOS Ventura 13 or later, use the steps below.
- Choose Apple menu > System Settings.
- Click General in the sidebar.
- Click AirDrop & Continuity (some versions say AirDrop & Handoff).
- Turn on Allow Handoff between this Mac and your iCloud devices.
On an earlier macOS, choose Apple menu > System Preferences, click General, and select Allow Handoff between this Mac and your iCloud devices.
| Device | Path to the Handoff setting | 
|---|---|
| Mac, macOS Ventura 13 or later | System Settings > General > AirDrop & Continuity > Allow Handoff between this Mac and your iCloud devices | 
| Mac, earlier macOS | System Preferences > General > Allow Handoff between this Mac and your iCloud devices | 
| iPhone or iPad | Settings > General > AirPlay & Continuity (or AirPlay & Handoff) > Handoff | 
| Apple Watch | Apple Watch app on iPhone > General > Enable Handoff | 
Step 2: Check the Apple Account on each device
Both features only work between devices signed in with the same Apple Account.
On the Mac, look at the account name at the top of System Settings, and on the iPhone look at your name at the top of Settings.
If the accounts differ, sign out of the wrong one and sign in with the account you use everywhere else.
Step 3: Turn on Bluetooth and Wi-Fi
Apple says Bluetooth and Wi-Fi must be on for every device.
If the Mac cannot connect to a Bluetooth accessory or a network at all, our guides to Bluetooth not connecting on a Mac and Wi-Fi not working on a Mac cover that first.
Step 4: Keep the devices close and unlocked
Keep the devices within 30 feet (10 meters) of each other.
For Handoff, Apple also says the source device should be unlocked and near the other device, with the task still showing and the app open in front.

NEWS 2026-11-18 iThinkDifferent (iPhone Duo Gets Easier to Use One-Handed in iOS 27.3):
iOS 27.3 improves iPhone Duo one-handed use with a camera-based unlock and a Reachability mode that slides the screen sideways. A third setting locks the phone when you fold it shut, so the folded iPhone Duo no longer hands your unlocked session to the outer display.
Face unlock and the lock setting came with iOS 27.3 beta 2 on November 16, while Reachability has been in the first beta since November 3. Most of the changes target the 5.4-inch outer display you use when the phone is folded.
Folded iPhone Duo Gets Two Lock Options
Face unlock reads your face through the front camera on the outer display, so you can open the folded phone by looking at it. The iPhone Duo has Touch ID in the side button and no Face ID hardware, so the camera option sits next to Touch ID rather than replacing it. You turn on face unlock in Settings under Touch ID & Passcode, on the same screen as Rest Finger to Open and Unlock with Apple Watch.
What face unlock cannot do
- Apple Pay, passwords and app sign-ins still need Touch ID or your passcode, because face unlock opens the phone and nothing else.
- After 45 minutes of inactivity, you need to enter Touch ID or your passcode before face unlock works again.
- Face unlock only works on the folded phone, so the inner display still unlocks with Touch ID or your passcode.
Close to lock is a separate opt-in setting under Display & Brightness. The default still hands your unlocked apps to the outer display when you fold the phone, and the setting replaces that handoff with a lock. Before this setting, the closest option was a Shortcuts automation on the open or close trigger that iOS 27.2 added.
iPhone Duo One-Handed Use Gets Easier
iPhone Duo Reachability slides the screen sideways, where Reachability on other iPhones pulls it down. A short swipe to the side shifts the content left or right toward your thumb, and you turn the feature on or off in Settings under Accessibility. The iPhone Duo went on sale on October 23 without Reachability, and Apple had said it would arrive later this year.
The beta also changes the keyboard on the outer display, which gets narrower keys and a slightly smaller font to make typing with one hand easier.
Registered developers can install the developer beta from Settings, General, Software Update, and iOS 27.3 is expected to reach all iPhone users in December.

SOURCE support.apple.com (Set up iPhone Handoff - Apple Support):
Set up iPhone Handoff
iPhone Handoff lets you use one phone number between two devices, so you can switch between them whenever you want. It makes it easy to move back and forth between devices optimized for the moment — like weekday business or weekend adventures.
About iPhone Handoff
When you use iPhone Handoff, your calls1, voicemail, messages (iMessage, RCS, or SMS), and Find My location automatically move to whichever iPhone you're using at the time. This allows you to pick up either device and stay reachable on the same number. Simply unlock whichever device you want to use and you're ready to go. Other data synced with iCloud will automatically update across your devices. Third-party apps work across both devices, following each app's own syncing behavior2.
You can set up iPhone Handoff during or after your new iPhone setup. Carrier fees might apply when enrolling in iPhone Handoff. Contact your carrier for more details.
What you need
- Two devices running iOS 27 or later that are: 
  - Connected to Wi-Fi
  - Sharing the same Apple Account
  - Using Messages in iCloud to ensure messages sync
  - Signed into FaceTime and iMessage with the same Apple Account
- An eSIM from a carrier that supports iPhone Handoff: 
  - USA: T-Mobile
  - Germany: Telekom
  - United Kingdom: EE
Set up iPhone Handoff
You can set up iPhone Handoff when setting up a new iPhone, or later in Settings.
After iPhone Handoff is set up, one iPhone becomes the main iPhone and the other iPhone becomes the secondary iPhone that shares the number. Your main iPhone should be the one you use most often. Some carrier services, like Call Forwarding and Caller ID, and carrier account management can only be managed on your main iPhone. Contact your carrier for more details.
To move between your main iPhone and secondary iPhone, simply unlock the device that you want to start using — your phone number will automatically become active on that device. The iPhone that you switched from will display an arrow icon at the top of your screen. The iPhone that you switched to will display the message “Switched to this iPhone” at the top of your screen to confirm it’s now active. Your phone number will only be active on one iPhone at a time when using iPhone Handoff. To stay in control of which iPhone is active, keep a passcode enabled on your iPhone and keep it private.
Pair your Apple Watch to the iPhone you use the most.
iPhone Handoff doesn't switch your Apple Watch to your other iPhone. If you are wearing an Apple Watch without the paired iPhone nearby, it can connect via Wi-Fi or cellular (if activated). If neither is available, calls, messages, notifications, certain health and fitness features, Siri AI, or other app experiences relayed from your paired iPhone may not be available.
You can add payment cards to Wallet during setup and they work on both devices. You can add a car key after setup and then share it across devices. Some Wallet items, such as certain transit passes, IDs, or corporate badges, might only work on one device at a time.
Set up iPhone Handoff during new iPhone setup
When setting up a new iPhone, you can choose to activate iPhone Handoff if supported by your carrier. Following setup, your new iPhone becomes the main iPhone and your current iPhone becomes the secondary iPhone sharing that number.
Before you start, place your main iPhone next to your secondary iPhone so that you can see the prompts from both devices.

SOURCE theapplepost.com (iPhone Handoff: Everything you need to know | The Apple Post):
iPhone Handoff is one of the more unusual additions to iOS 27, allowing the same phone number to be used across two iPhones without repeatedly transferring an eSIM between them.
Apple has now published detailed support information explaining exactly how the feature works, what moves between devices, what happens with Apple Watch and Wallet, and some important limitations users should know before setting it up.
At its simplest, iPhone Handoff lets you keep a main iPhone and a secondary iPhone sharing the same number. Unlocking whichever iPhone you want to use makes that device active, while the other becomes inactive on the cellular network.
What moves between your iPhones?
When you switch devices, calls, voicemail, iMessage, RCS and SMS/MMS messages follow the active iPhone. Your Find My location also moves to the iPhone you are currently using.
Data stored in iCloud continues to sync normally between the two devices. Third-party apps can work across both iPhones too, although their behavior depends on the individual app. Some apps may sign you out when another device signs in, while banking apps may require additional authentication.
Only one iPhone can have the shared phone number active at any one time. After switching, iOS displays a “Switched to this iPhone” message to confirm which device is currently active.
What you need to use iPhone Handoff
Both iPhones need to be running iOS 27 or later, connected to Wi-Fi during setup and signed into the same Apple Account. Messages in iCloud must be enabled, and both devices need to be signed into FaceTime and iMessage using the same Apple Account.
You also need an eSIM from a carrier supporting iPhone Handoff. Carrier availability is currently limited, and carrier charges can apply.
The Apple Post previously reported that T-Mobile will charge $5 per month for iPhone Handoff in the United States. Apple lists T-Mobile as the supported U.S. carrier and Telekom as the supported carrier in Germany.
Main and secondary iPhones
During setup, one device is designated as the main iPhone and the other becomes the secondary iPhone. Apple recommends making the phone you use most frequently your main device.
Some carrier functions remain tied to the main iPhone even when the secondary device is active. Apple says this can include Call Forwarding, Caller ID and carrier account management.
If you enable iPhone Handoff while setting up a new iPhone, the new device becomes the main iPhone by default and the existing device becomes the secondary iPhone. The arrangement can also be configured later through Settings > Cellular.
What happens to Apple Watch?
Apple Watch does not automatically follow whichever iPhone is active through Handoff. It remains paired with its existing iPhone, so Apple recommends pairing your watch with whichever iPhone you use most often.
If the paired iPhone is unavailable, Apple Watch can continue using Wi-Fi or cellular where available. Without either connection, some calls, messages, notifications, health and fitness features, Siri AI and other experiences relayed through the paired iPhone may not be available.
What happens to Apple Wallet?
Payment cards can be added during setup and used on both iPhones. Car keys can also be added and shared between the devices.
There are exceptions. Apple says some Wallet items, including certain transit passes, IDs and corporate badges, may only work on one iPhone at a time.

SOURCE macrumors.com (iPhone Handoff in iOS 27: How It Works, Pricing, and Carrier ...):
Apple in iOS 27 introduced iPhone Handoff, a new eSIM feature that allows you to use the same number on two iPhones and seamlessly swap between them. The number is only active on one iPhone at a time, so it's not like having two independently active lines.
It's also different from Apple's existing Handoff feature for continuing an app task on another Apple device. Here's what you need to know about the new iPhone Handoff feature.
What Moves Between the Two iPhones?
When you switch phones with iPhone Handoff, your calls, voicemail, messages (including iMessage, RCS, SMS, and MMS) and Find My location move to the active iPhone. You'll see a "Switched to this iPhone" message on the screen to confirm the change.
Other data synced with iCloud will automatically update across your devices, and third-party apps work across both devices, though some third-party apps may require a separate sign-in or take time to sync. Any banking apps you use may also ask you to approve access on the other device.
What Do You Need for iPhone Handoff?
Both iPhones must be running iOS 27 or later. They'll also need to be:
- Connected to Wi-Fi
- Sharing the same Apple Account
- Using Messages in iCloud for messages sync
- Signed into FaceTime and iMessage with the same Apple Account
iPhone Handoff works with Dual SIM as long as both eSIMs are from carriers that support iPhone Handoff. Both eSIMs must be set up for iPhone Handoff separately, one at a time. Once set up, both eSIMs switch together simultaneously when you unlock your iPhone.
Which Carriers Support iPhone Handoff?
iPhone Handoff is available through T-Mobile in the United States and Telekom in Germany. Verizon (U.S.) and EE (U.K.) will support iPhone Handoff later this year.
AT&T has so far not committed to supporting iPhone Handoff, with a company spokesperson recently pointing to the carrier's existing eSIM activation and transfer options instead.
How Much Does iPhone Handoff Cost?
T-Mobile is charging customers $5 per month to use iPhone Handoff.
In Germany, Deutsche Telekom is charging €6.95 per month for iPhone Handoff, but only on plans that do not already include multi-SIM functionality. An added multi-SIM costs €6.95 per month (one is included with the current MagentaMobil L plan and two with XL).
No other carriers have announced pricing yet.
How Do You Set It Up?
iPhone Handoff can be enabled when setting up a new iPhone. At the "Set Up Cellular" screen, choose "Use Number on This iPhone and Another," then follow the prompts on both phones.
If both iPhones are already set up, open Settings ➝ Cellular on the phone you want to add. Tap Set Up Cellular or Add eSIM, choose Use Number on This iPhone and Another, and follow the prompts. You then get to choose which device is your main iPhone (ideally, the one you use most often) and which is your secondary iPhone.
After setup, unlock either phone to make your number active on it.
What Should You Know Before Switching?
If you have an Apple Watch, it won't switch its pairing to the other device when your phone number moves, so make sure you pair it with the iPhone you expect to use most. Also, some Wallet items, including certain transit passes and IDs, may only work on one device at a time.
Carrier account management and some services like Call Forwarding and Caller ID will remain tied to your main iPhone.

SOURCE trustedreviews.com (What is iPhone Handoff and why would you want it?):
If you’ve got two iPhones in frequent use, then you’ll understand the frustration of constantly needing to carrying both around.That’s where iPhone Handoff comes in.
It’s a niche problem, sure, but iPhone Handoff promises to make it much easier to ensure you won’t miss notifications across your two iPhones. But how does iPhone Handoff work and how do you use it? Is the feature even available in the UK?
We explain all you need to know about iPhone Handoff, including where you can find the feature and how to either enable or disable it.
Make sure you also visit our round-up of the best iPhones and best smartphones too.
What is iPhone Handoff?
iPhone Handoff allows you to use one phone number between two handsets, meaning you can easily switch from one to the other whenever you need. This will especially suit those who have a separate work handset from their personal one, or perhaps creators who have a phone specifically for shooting content and don’t want to carry their usual handset around.
iPhone Handoff supports calls, voicemail, messages and Find My across the two handsets, with the latter automatically moving to whichever iPhone you’re using at the time. In addition, other data synced with iCloud and third-party apps will automatically update across the two devices.
What do you need to set up iPhone Handoff?
To get started, you’ll need two iPhones that are both running iOS 27, are connected to Wi-Fi and share the same Apple account. You’ll also need an eSIM from a carrier that supports iPhone Handoff. At the time of writing, supported carriers include T-Mobile in the USA and Telekom in Germany. EE has also confirmed that it will support iPhone Handoff in the UK but is yet to specify the exact launch date.
Still using a physical SIM? Visit our guide on how to turn your SIM into an eSIM on an iPhone to see the process and follow our steps.
Otherwise, you can choose to enable iPhone Handoff when you’re either setting up a new phone or after the fact. Choosing the latter option will allow you to pick which of your two devices becomes the primary iPhone, while the former will automatically enable the new iPhone to become your main model.
How to set up iPhone Handoff
The steps on how to enable iPhone Handoff will vary depending on whether or not you’re doing so while setting up an iPhone. Regardless of which way round you’re doing it, make sure you have both iPhones turned on and sat next to each other.
If you’re setting up a new iPhone while enabling iPhone Handoff, then the steps are pretty simple:
- Start setting up your main iPhone as normal
- On Set Up Cellular, tap the Use Number on This Phone and Another
- Tap Continue
- Review the details and tap Continue
- Follow the prompts on both devices
Otherwise, if you’re enabling iPhone Handoff on devices that have already been set-up, then the process is slightly different:
- Open the Settings app and tap Cellular
- Tap Set Up Cellular or Add eSIM
- Select Use Number on This Phone and Another
- Tap Continue
- Select an iPhone and tap Continue
- Follow the onscreen prompts on both devices
Why would you need iPhone Handoff
Admittedly, not many of us have two iPhones in constant rotation, so this feature might not be one that’s used often. However, those with a work iPhone and personal iPhone will undoubtedly benefit from being able to carry just one handset out with them, without needing to worry that they’ll miss a call or other notification.
